text:
A Theory About Mitya's Scarf

I made a video on this theory, but here's a text version as well as an analysis of their personality. (also I refer to the scarf as they/them and not 'it')

Basically, from 7.0 and Mitya's drip marketing it's fairly reasonable to assume that his scarf has a will of their own and is sentient. They're very close to Mitya, being referred to as his 'dear companion', and seem to be a bit more responsible than him. They keep Mitya quiet when he starts to talk about Project Stuzha, and Valeriy seems to trust them enough to want to give them greater clearance (this part of Mitya's drip marketing was also the final thing that made me certain that the scarf is sentient, since Valeriy would have no reason to say that if the scarf was just an extension of Mitya's will or a mere object)

However, the scarf is also a patron of the arts! They pay more attention to the performances than Mitya and remembered the actual songs that Vodyanitsa sang. i point this out in the video, but that scene with Vodyanitsa is the best display of the scarf's personality. They get overwhelmed with frustration at one point and can't form a shape for a moment, and they also poke fun at Mitya after Vodyanitsa calls him out.

Also, during the fight with Ronova the scarf isn't 'awake' at first and only reacts when Mitya is directly attacked. I feel like this is intentional since we've seen the scarf active but not doing anything before, and it's different than when they're 'asleep' and completely limp. When they are actually fighting, they're incredibly in sync with Mitya, with both of them reacting to each other instantly. I personally think that there's some bond allowing them to sense each other's emotions or something like that.

So, here's the theory itself;

Mitya's scarf is an angel. they have a similar color to Seelies and we know that angels (or at least their remains) can bond to human souls, so if the scarf bonded to Mitya somehow it would explain the mark in his hair. Angels are closely tied to the Ley Lines, so it would make sense that the scarf wouldn't count towards the totals in the theater, which would be why Ronova didn't care about them.

This is a bit more of a headcanon, but I think it would be interesting if the angel the would become the scarf was a part of Koitar’s rebellion. That would give them a lot of motivation to make sure the Tsarita's plan to take down the Heavenly principles succeeds. As a bonus, them keeping Mitya on track and focused could also be a form of 'guidance'.

Some ideas about how they became a scarf now! One idea is that when they chose to give up their power in exchange for keeping their wisdom, they were able to sacrifice even more and lost the chance of even keeping an intangible Seelie from, with the tradeoff of keeping their mind and knowledge fully intact. Nicole has a teapot line where she says that all the angels used to be connected to a 'library' of Celestia's knowledge, and that they 'lost their keys' after the rebellion. She also says that there are some angels who may have been able to keep their access, so it'd be interesting if the scarf still has that connection.

Another theory is that they were able to keep or regain their intelligence as a Seelie, similar to Mr Nine, and seek out researchers to give them a better body. My first instinct was Hvergelmir, since they have zero regards for unethical experiments or possibly angering the gods. There’s also the chance that the Seelie didn't intentionally seek them out and was instead captured and experimented on, which would also be on brand for them. Or instead of Hvergelmir, it was Mitya himself who created the scarf body and possibly tied them to his soul, or Mitya was also experimented on.

That's the theory! I know it's incredibly unlikely to be true in any way, but it was really fun to ruminate on. I've been avoiding story or lore leaks so I have no idea if there's anything that's been leaked that directly counteracts this.

The thing I dislike most about Sumerus stories… ... is the amount of downright evil people not getting their comeuppance. It happened 3 times now already (spoiler for Khvarena Of Good And Evil is hidden) and it's really bugging me at this point.

- Azar. The guy responsible for locking the entirety of Sumeru into the Sabzeruz festival samsara, which very nearly led to at least one casualty which he was more than willing to take in stride and all around a nasty piece of work in person. Gets 'banished' by Nahida to who knows where. Sure, might be he lost his cushy position, but for all we know, he could be having a grand old time whereever he is.

- Masseira. Guy emotionally abused his daughter, turning her into a tool for his hunt and as soon as it seemed she was starting to grow independent thanks to the Travellers influence, he makes her fight them to the death while running and hiding out in some safehouse while leaving us a taunting letter. I was honestly lowkey hoping we'd come across him in the new area, but nope, no such luck.

- Nasejuna: Blatantly obvious bad guy from the start, nobody grows wise to his increasingly insistent demands to just hand over the precious artifacts until *gasp shock* he turns on the group, reveals his allegiance to the Abyss Order, acts as the flunky to an actually threatening member of said faction... aaaaaand then apparently manages to flee, never to be seen or heard from again and nobody really cares to look for them.

Sure, they all lost to some degree, but we were robbed of the satisfaction of seeing them confronted with their failure and facing any real consequences. At most, they're setbacks, they could easily come back to haunt the Traveller in the future, so not just from a story perspective it's unfulfilling, but it's also a serious flaw of the Traveller to not follow up on such loose ends.

text:
Rune Inscription in Snezhnaya

In the latest 7.1 Archon Quest Pierro summons a nail with his delusion.We can see that there are some Ancient Runes in Teyvat's alphabet on the circles that he summons, and I managed to translate some of it looking at Elder and Younger Futhark, the runic alphabet used for Proto Norse, Old Norse and various other Scandinavian languages.The transcription in latin alphabet from Teyvat's Ancient runes is:

"Alugisalaz gagaga ek erilaz wrta naudir ger ernaeppa koste yr"

Now, I found two inscriptions:

"ᚾ Nauðr gerer næppa koste", found in a runic poem about the n-rune ᚾ, which means "need" or "distress". It translates to "Constraint gives scant choice".

"*ek erilaz āsugīsalas muha haitē, gagaga", found on a lance shaft named Kragehul I. It translates to "I, the erilaz of Āsugīsalaz, am called Muha, ga-ga-ga!", but considering only the part appearing on Pierro's cricles we would have instead "The erilaz of Asugisalaz, gagaga". Erilaz means "magician" or "rune master", Asugisalaz is composed of ansu-, "god", and gisalaz, "hostage", and lastly gagaga may be a ritual chant.

The only two words that are missing from this are "yr" and "wrta". I found that "yr" is a rune in Younger Futhark meaning "yew", but i can't find anything on "wrta".I thought I could mix them, and found the Old-English word "wyrhta", meaning "worker, maker". I also found the word "Wyrd", which is concept related to fate and destiny.

I am in no way knowledgable about runes, Futhark or Old English, and only found these things searching on wikipedia. So if someone has any idea how to translate these two words please do share with me :)

text:
[Theory] Could Ronova’s death return the Authority of Death to Columbina? The connection between the Four Shades, the Three Moons, and Celestia’s system

I’ve been thinking about Ronova’s death, Columbina becoming the Trilune Goddess, and the original relationship between the Four Shades and the Three Moon Goddesses. I wonder if we’re looking at something bigger than the death of one of the Shades.

My theory is that the Authorities of Life, Death, Time, and Space originally belonged to the Three Moon Goddesses, and the Heavenly Principles took control of those authorities and redistributed them among the Four Shades. If that’s true, could Ronova’s defeat eventually allow the Authority of Death to return to its original lunar source through Columbina?

I know this is speculative, but there are several pieces of lore that make me think this possibility deserves discussion.

1. The Four Authorities may originate from an older cosmic order

The lore surrounding the Three Moons connects them to the fundamental authorities of Life, Death, Time, and Space. These are also associated with the Four Shades of the Heavenly Principles.

This raises an important question: were these authorities originally created as part of the Heavenly Principles’ system, or did the Heavenly Principles take control of powers that already belonged to an older cosmic order?

If the Three Moon Goddesses originally held these authorities, then the Four Shades possessing them today could represent a redistribution of power rather than its original ownership.In other words, the Heavenly Principles may have changed who governs these laws without necessarily being their original source.

I think this distinction is important because the current holder of an authority isn’t necessarily its original owner.

2. Ronova’s Authority of Death may originally have belonged to the lunar order

Ronova, the Ruler of Death, is one of the Four Shades created by the Primordial One. Her authority governs death and is connected to the curses imposed on the people of Khaenri’ah.

However, if the Authority of Death originally belonged to the Three Moon Goddesses, then Ronova’s position might be the result of the Heavenly Principles redistributing that authority after the Moons’ downfall.That would make Ronova the current holder of a power that originated elsewhere.

This is the foundation of my theory: Ronova may have exercised the Authority of Death on behalf of the Heavenly Principles, even though that authority originally belonged to the lunar order.

Of course, this depends on whether the lore establishes that the Moons were the original owners of these authorities, rather than merely associating them with the same cosmic principles.

3. Columbina becoming the Trilune Goddess could be more significant than we realize

The Three Moon Goddesses transferred their lunar powers to Columbina, allowing her to become the Trilune Goddess.What interests me is that Columbina didn’t simply gain another elemental ability. She became the successor to the combined lunar authority of the Three Moons. If the Authority of Death originally belonged to the lunar order, Columbina could potentially be the one capable of reclaiming it.

I am not saying that becoming the Trilune Goddess automatically gives her all four authorities. The game would need to establish whether her current authority includes the ability to reclaim powers that the Heavenly Principles redistributed to the Four Shades.

However, her ascension makes the possibility particularly interesting. If the original lunar order is being restored, Columbina could represent more than a new goddess occupying an old position. She could be the means through which the authority of the Moon Goddesses is restored.

4. The Tsaritsa’s trap reveals something important about Ronova’s authority

This is where I think the theory becomes more interesting.During the Archon Quest, Rhinedottir and Ronova had an arrangement involving death and resurrection. Ronova could kill people, and Rhinedottir could revive them before Celestia’s monitoring detected the unauthorized deaths.The Tsaritsa disrupted this arrangement by using the six Gnoses to interfere with the passage of time in the chamber where she confronted Rhinedottir. Rhinedottir could no longer complete the resurrections within the required window, allowing Celestia to detect Ronova’s transgression.

The Heavenly Principles then reclaimed Ronova’s authority.What stands out to me is that Ronova lost her authority before her final defeat. Its removal was a consequence of Celestia’s intervention, not simply the result of Ronova dying.

This raises a question: what exactly happened to the authority after it was reclaimed? Did Celestia permanently absorb it? Did the authority remain as a separate power under Celestia’s control? Or was Ronova merely stripped of her right to wield it?

The quest establishes that Celestia can revoke a Shade’s authority, but I don’t think that alone answers what happens to the authority’s original source. If Death originally belonged to the lunar order, could the Heavenly Principles’ control over it be temporary or reversible?And if Ronova’s defeat destabilizes the current system, could the authority eventually return to its original source?

I think this is an important distinction because the question isn’t simply whether Columbina can inherit Ronova’s power. It’s whether the Heavenly Principles can permanently prevent the lunar order from reclaiming something that originally belonged to it.

5. Rhinedottir and Naberius’s Heart: can power associated with a Shade be acquired by someone else?

Another detail I think is relevant is Rhinedottir’s acquisition of the Heart of Naberius.

Naberius is associated with the Authority of Life, and Rhinedottir’s discovery of the Heart of Naberius is central to her alchemical research and the creation of Albedo.The important point here is that Rhinedottir obtained something associated with a higher being and used it in her own work involving the creation of life.

I want to be careful not to equate the Heart of Naberius with the complete cosmic Authority of Life. Acquiring the Heart does not automatically prove that Rhinedottir inherited Naberius’s entire authority in the same way that Neuvillette regained the Hydro Dragon Sovereign’s authority.

Nevertheless, the connection raises an interesting question: are the powers of the Four Shades inseparable from their holders, or can some part of those powers exist independently and be transferred, acquired, or reclaimed?

If power associated with Life can be obtained through the Heart of Naberius, perhaps the authorities are not always inseparable from the beings who currently wield them.This could be relevant to Ronova. If the Authority of Death can exist independently of her, then her defeat does not necessarily mean the authority disappears. It could remain under Celestia’s control, become unassigned, or potentially return to its original source.

Rhinedottir’s case doesn’t prove that the lunar order can reclaim Death, but it gives us another reason to investigate how authorities and their vessels actually work.

6. The Hydro Sovereign precedent: original ownership matters

Neuvillette’s restoration is another comparison worth considering.

When Focalors destroyed the Hydro Archon’s divine throne, the Hydro authority was returned to Neuvillette, its original Sovereign. This demonstrated that an authority could be separated from its current holder and restored to its original owner through a specific mechanism.

I know Ronova’s situation is different. She is a Shade, not an Archon holding a Sovereign’s stolen elemental authority. Therefore, we cannot simply assume that her authority will follow the same rules.

However, Neuvillette’s case establishes an important principle: the current holder of an authority and its original owner do not necessarily have to be the same being.If the lunar order originally held the Authority of Death, could something similar eventually happen to it?Perhaps the authority must first be released from Celestia’s control. Perhaps Columbina would have to perform some action to reclaim it. Or perhaps the rules governing the Shades’ authorities are entirely different.

But I don’t think we should dismiss the possibility just because Ronova’s situation differs from Neuvillette’s.

7. Could this connect to Ronova’s final gift and the worldwide anomaly?

I also wonder whether Ronova’s final act is connected to the larger changes happening to the Celestial Nails.Before her death, Ronova called her final act a “gift.” She also fused EITR with the Nail of Retribution, after which the Nails began behaving abnormally.

EITR is associated with modified Light Realm power and creation, while Holy Soil has connections to the primordial elemental environment and the difficulties it can cause for human life.

Could Ronova’s action be interfering with the system the Heavenly Principles established to regulate Teyvat?I don’t think we can definitively say that the Nails are simply seals that will be removed. Their functions are more complex than that. But their abnormal behavior raises the possibility that the existing order is being disrupted.

If the Heavenly Principles’ system is weakening, perhaps the consequences extend beyond the Nails themselves. Could the same disruption eventually affect the distribution of the Four Authorities?

This also makes Ronova’s final words more ambiguous. She previously helped Natlan and the Lord of the Night establish a system that protected humanity, despite the risks associated with her position.

That doesn’t prove her final action was benevolent. She may have intended to make humanity suffer. But it does make me wonder whether her last act could have consequences that go beyond her personal intentions.

Perhaps the worldwide anomaly and the potential restoration of the lunar authorities are connected to a larger change in Teyvat’s cosmic order.

8. My central question: can the Heavenly Principles permanently keep the authorities they took from the Moon Goddesses?

Putting these pieces together, my theory is:

The Three Moon Goddesses originally possessed the authorities of Life, Death, Time, and Space.

After the Moons’ downfall, the Heavenly Principles took control of these authorities and redistributed them among the Four Shades.

Ronova’s authority was subsequently subject to Celestia’s control, as demonstrated when it was revoked during the Tsaritsa’s trap.

Rhinedottir’s acquisition of the Heart of Naberius raises questions about whether power associated with a Shade can be separated from its holder.

Columbina has now become the Trilune Goddess, potentially restoring the lunar order in a way that could matter for the fate of the original authorities.

If these premises are correct, then Ronova’s defeat could be significant not merely because a Shade has fallen, but because it may create an opportunity for the original lunar authority to be reclaimed.

I’m not saying that Columbina automatically inherits Death when Ronova dies. The authority may still be controlled by the Heavenly Principles, and the rules governing the Four Shades may prevent it from returning to the Moon Goddesses.

But I think the possibility deserves consideration.

What if Columbina’s ascension as the Trilune Goddess is not just the restoration of the Moon Goddesses themselves, but also the beginning of the restoration of the authorities that originally belonged to them?

And if that’s the case, could Ronova’s defeat and the worldwide anomaly be two parts of the same larger event—the gradual destabilization of the Heavenly Principles’ order and the return of an older cosmic system?

I’d love to hear what other people think, especially if there are lore passages that contradict this interpretation or clarify what happens to an authority after Celestia reclaims it.
